title: Wayfinder Groove: Console navigation IA & workspace switcher redesign
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) customers need quicker, less error-prone ways to switch context, understand which model/route is live, and find per-route cost/latency dashboards. Current sidebar and workspace-switcher interactions are overloaded: deep nested menus, inconsistent affordances for rollouts, and no persistent 'active route' surface. This leads to support tickets and slow task flows for Platform and Customer Success when diagnosing regressions.

Goal: Produce an information architecture and interaction model for the Console that: 1) reduces steps to switch workspace or pivot to a different deployment (hosted/dedicated/private); 2) surfaces per-route cost & latency lenses with clear lineage to rollouts and model versions; 3) supports canary/A-B rollouts and graceful fallbacks in the navigation experience; 4) fits in the existing left-rail real estate while enabling a compact/pinned variant for power users.

Success metrics (targeted):
- Median time to switch workspace reduced from ~9s to <4s in prototype tests.
- Number of clicks to reach route-level cost dashboard reduced to <=2 from top-level nav.
- Usability score for rollout discovery >= 80 (System Usability Scale) in quick tests.

Constraints & considerations:
- Must not require backend changes for initial MVP; use Console routing and query params to represent workspace/model context.
- Accessibility: keyboard shortcuts and ARIA roles mandatory.
- Internationalization-ready labels.
- Work with Product/Engineering to avoid breaking existing deep links (support legacy route params).

Proposed concepts (explored in prototypes):
1) 'Lanepath' Left Rail: persistent compact rail with three vertical zones (Tenant, Workspace, Routes). Hover-expands to full rail. Routes show live status pill (green/orange/red), cost delta badge, and rollout indicator. Workspace switcher is a top-level chip that opens a contextual mini-map of workspaces.
2) 'Context Lens' Floating Panel: when selecting a route, a contextual lens slides from the right summarizing last 24h cost/latency, active model versions, and rollout policy controls (canary %, fallback). The lens is reachable with a keyboard shortcut and deep-linked URL.
3) 'Quick-Command Palette' Integration: a command palette that supports fast switching (type workspace name or route) and preview cards showing immediate cost and latency micro-metrics. Useful for SREs and power users.

Trade-offs considered:
- Compact rail vs full nav: compact saves screen real estate but requires strong discoverability cues. Chosen path: default compact with discoverability hotspots and an onboarding tooltip.
- Surface telemetry in nav vs in lens: telemetry in nav clutters primary surface; decided to show minimal badges in nav and full metrics in the Context Lens to balance density.

Artifacts & links: 
- Figma prototype (primary exploratory): https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/wayfinder-groove-console-ia (prototype frames: CompactRail, ContextLens, CommandPalette)
- Clickable InVision demo (usability script): https://invision.example.com/share/WAYFINDER
- PRD / design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Wayfinder+Groove+IA+Redesign
- Related engineering ticket for routing params: ENG-98120
- Usability test plan & task list (docs): https://docs.google.com/document/d/EXAMPLE-wayfinder-usability

Open questions for PM/Eng: 
- Do rollouts need write APIs from the Console MVP or will we show read-only rollout state initially? (PM preference: read-only for MVP)
- Confirm list of route-level telemetry we can surface without extra backend work (Product to confirm).
- Should workspaces support fuzzy search in the switcher or require exact matching? (Design recommends fuzzy + keyboard)

Next steps (planned):
- 2025-02-20 to 2025-02-28: iterate on rails and context lens based on internal design critique.
- 2025-03-02 to 2025-03-08: moderated usability testing with 6 participants (mix of PMs, SREs, and customers).
- 2025-03-09 to 2025-03-15: consolidate feedback, produce final handoff frames + annotated specs for Eng.

Deliverables: annotated Figma frames, interaction spec (keyboard shortcuts, ARIA mapping), handoff checklist, and usability report.
comments: 2025-02-19 — Aisha Khatri: Initial kickoff meeting with PM (Ravi) and Eng lead (Lina). Decided to avoid backend schema changes for MVP; we'll rely on query-string deep links. Captured blocker: rollout write API is not available in next sprint.
2025-02-22 — Ethan Morales: Posted first-round wireframes in Figma. Requested feedback on badge density for routes. Noted that Dedicated clusters need a visual namespace distinct from Hosted.

2025-02-25 — Lina Park (Eng): Reviewed prototype; asked for explicit mapping of legacy deep-links to new compact rail states. Agreed to implement adapter in console-router. Added ENG-98120 as dependency.

2025-03-02 — Usability session 1: 6 participants. Early findings: users discovered workspace switcher in 3.6s median with command palette enabled; some confusion between 'route' and 'deployment' labels. Action: rename 'Route' -> 'Route / Endpoint' and add hover help.
2025-03-04 — PM review (Ravi): Approved Context Lens read-only MVP. Asked to prioritize cost delta badge for top 3 most-used routes. Set stakeholder demo for 2025-03-18.
2025-03-05 — Design critique: team chose compact rail default with persistent microbadges and Context Lens. Ethan to produce annotated specs and small icon set for rollout states.
